name: orkestr Sandboxes

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go sandbox (metered on actual use)
modes.note: orkestr.eu/pricing (Sandboxes tab, JS bundle, 2026-09-28): vCPU EUR 0.045/hour, RAM EUR 0.015/GiB-hour, storage EUR 0.10/GB-month; sizes small 1 vCPU/1 GB, medium 2 vCPU/4 GB, large 4 vCPU/8 GB ('cost shown at full utilization'). Metered 'per second, on actual usage - real on-CPU time and working-set RAM, not the provisioned size'. Converted at 1.1378 USD/EUR (ECB 2026-09-28). Prices in EUR, VAT applied where required.

internet.allowlist: Curated 'restricted' mode: PyPI/pythonhosted, npm, Debian apt, GitHub/githubusercontent, model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Cohere, Groq, Hugging Face).

evidence.quote: open (full egress, paid tier with verified billing)
opt into a curated allowlist of dev hosts (PyPI, npm, GitHub, common LLM APIs), bring your own allowlist, or open egress when you need it.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: No card: 'EUR 5 credit, then it stops', 'Small only, 3 concurrent', '30-min sessions'. Trial only.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Card on file: 'EUR 25 credit, then metered', all sizes, concurrency 'High' (number not published), sessions 'Up to 24 h', 10 snapshots, own spend cap.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Dedicated EU nodes, custom limits + SLA, audit logs, SSO. Custom price.

caveats: Rates come from the Sandboxes tab of orkestr.eu/pricing (rendered from the site's JS bundle); the orkestr.eu/sandboxes page still says 'Published rates land once we have metered real workloads'. Treat as a published but early (beta) rate card. Billed on actual on-CPU time and working-set RAM, so idle sandboxes cost almost nothing. First 10 GB of held storage (snapshots + templates) free, then EUR 0.10/GB-month. Egress price unpublished; full egress needs a paid verified account.
Default network off; full egress needs paid verified account.
150–300 ms cold-start claims vary by page/template; no benchmark recorded.
Worked example assumes resources are released between active windows unless a retained-instance scenario is explicitly discussed.
VAT basis: Unknown: reviewed pricing source does not explicitly establish VAT/tax inclusion.
Residency: Provider claims code, memory, snapshots and environment remain EU; Falkenstein DE, Helsinki FI, Roubaix FR; DPA available. Not independently audited.

Billing-basis conflict: the pricing FAQ says sandboxes bill actual on-CPU time and working-set RAM (idle almost free), but orkestr.eu/docs/sandboxes says each sandbox is 'metered per second of wall-clock time it's alive (whether or not the workload is busy)'. Idle-heavy estimates may be understated until the provider resolves this.

fleet.verification: Verified email earns starter credit, no card; card unlocks all sandbox sizes and paid metering.
fleet.notes: Sandbox PAYG is independent of Platform subscription. Platform PR-preview concurrent deployments (1/5) are not Sandbox runtime quotas. No numeric new-account sandbox count or increase path found.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: on_timeout	string	What happens at the deadline: kill (default) terminates the sandbox; pause snapshots it so a later /resume continues where it left off.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in per sandbox at create (on_timeout=pause; default is kill). Triggered by the lifetime deadline; snapshot captures memory + disk (running processes resume). Pairs with auto_resume=true, which resumes automatically on the next exec/file call or preview-URL HTTP request. Free tier falls back to terminate when at its snapshot cap (1).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/pause snapshots the sandbox and stops the compute meter. ... POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/resume restores from the most recent snapshot for that sandbox. ... The snapshot is consumed by the resume - pause again to take a new one
snapshot_on_demand.note: On-demand snapshot is pause-style: memory + disk captured (security page: 'the VM's memory and disk state are captured into a snapshot'), sandbox is suspended, and the snapshot is single-use, restoring the same sandbox only. No fork / boot-new-machines-from-snapshot documented; custom templates are built from a base image + recipe, not captured from a running sandbox. Retention 7 d free / 30 d carded / no expiry enterprise.

harness_api.quote:
result = sbx.exec(
    'npx claude -p "Run the test suite and fix the first failing test" '
    "--output-format json --dangerously-skip-permissions",
harness_api.note: The official Claude Code guide drives the agent through the generic exec API (npm install, then claude -p / --resume via exec); no dedicated harness API. Separately, orkestr 'Workers' (preview) run orkestr's own ops agent on its hosted runtime with your model key (objective, skills, memory, approvals, run transcripts), but that is a platform-ops agent product, not a harness API for sandboxes.

egress_allowlist.quote: When you pass allow_domains, those domains become the entire allowlist for that sandbox.
egress_allowlist.note: Three modes per sandbox: off (default, no network device), restricted (HTTPS-only forward proxy with curated default allowlist or custom allow_domains; no raw sockets/DNS), open. Enforced by a provider-side proxy; allowlist can be baked into a template. Hostname-level only; 'Custom egress allowlist: yes' on all tiers (limits page), though API ref says '(paid plans)'.

egress_http_rules.quote: Entries are bare hostnames - no scheme, port, path or wildcard.
egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist is hostname-only (HTTPS port 443); no method/path/header rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote: Pass preview_auth=True at create (previewAuth: true in JS) and the sandbox's preview URLs stop being public: every request must carry the minted preview_auth_token or the edge returns 401.
ingress_rules.note: Ports are exposed per port via get_host(port) at <port>-<id>.sbx.orkestr.run; public (unguessable URL) by default, token-gated with preview_auth. Needs networked mode + card on file. No IP allowlists documented.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is its own VM with its own kernel ('not a container sharing a host kernel'); recipe steps run as root and apt-get works at run time, so root is available. Egress policy is enforced outside the VM regardless (off = no NIC; restricted = proxy).

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets you inject (as env vars or files) are visible to whatever code runs in that sandbox - including code a model wrote.
secret_proxy.note: Sandbox secrets are env vars/files inside the VM (kept in memory, persisted inside pause snapshots). The Claude Code guide passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as an env var. (Workers product keeps git credentials in the control plane, but that is not a sandbox egress proxy.)

volume_attach.quote: A persistent volume is a named disk that survives a sandbox and follows you to the next one. Attach it and it mounts at /persist
volume_attach.note: ext4 disk local to the host, checkpointed to EU object storage; default 10 GB, max 100 GB per volume; 1/10/50 volumes and 10 GB/200 GB/2 TB total per tier; billed GB-month on provisioned size; optional max_lifetime auto-destroy.

volume_shared.quote: A volume can back only one running (or paused) sandbox at a time. Attaching a volume that's already in use returns a 409 volume_in_use
volume_shared.note: Single writer by design (ext4 RW); no read-only multi-attach or shared FS documented.

isolation.quote: Every sandbox is its own virtual machine with its own kernel, not a container sharing a host kernel. There is no shared container runtime and no syscall surface between tenants.
isolation.note: Docs describe a per-sandbox VM with its own kernel/rootfs/network stack but never name the hypervisor (no Firecracker/cloud-hypervisor/QEMU mention found), so mapped to the generic dedicated-vm value.

image_oci.quote: Build once with a base image + a recipe (via the console, REST API, or MCP)... orkestr boots a short-lived build VM from your base image with a writable root filesystem, runs each recipe step in order, and captures the result as a new image
image_oci.note: Custom templates are base image + shell recipe, not an arbitrary imported Docker/OCI image.

desktop.quote: orkestr Sandboxes are hardware-isolated, ephemeral Linux VMs you can spin up from any agent loop. Designed for AI agents that need to run untrusted code, build artifacts, run tests, or operate a stateful development environment
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (headless code-exec sandbox, no VNC/RDP/desktop stream documented).

browser.quote: Available bases: python-3.12, python-3.12-bare, code-interpreter, node-22, debian-12
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed/real browser is documented among base images or features.

computer_use.quote: orkestr Sandboxes are hardware-isolated, ephemeral Linux VMs you can spin up from any agent loop.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot/click desktop-driving API found.

anti_bot.quote: orkestr Sandboxes are hardware-isolated, ephemeral Linux VMs you can spin up from any agent loop.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (generic Linux code-exec sandbox, not a browser/scraping product).

captcha_solving.quote: orkestr Sandboxes are hardware-isolated, ephemeral Linux VMs you can spin up from any agent loop.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: the sandbox fleet today runs in three regions across three countries and two providers: fsn1 Falkenstein, Germany - Hetzner Online GmbH; hel1 Helsinki, Finland - Hetzner Online GmbH; rbx Roubaix, France - OVH SAS
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound traffic comes from Hetzner/OVH EU datacenter ranges; no residential/mobile IP option documented.

ssh.quote: `orkestr sbx shell <id>` Line-buffered interactive exec loop against a running sandbox. Type commands, each runs via exec
ssh.note: Access is via exec/run_code over the SDK, CLI, REST API or MCP - no SSH endpoint is documented anywhere in the sandbox docs.

fork.quote: `pause()` returns the sandbox id... Later, anywhere: sbx = Sandbox.resume(sandbox_id)
fork.note: Pause/resume restores the same sandbox from its own snapshot; no documented way to clone a sandbox into new, independent sandboxes.

fork_running.quote: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/resume restores from the most recent snapshot for that sandbox.
fork_running.note: No forking API; resume always targets the same sandbox id, and pausing stops it rather than leaving it running while cloned.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: On pause: the VM's memory and disk state are captured into a snapshot stored on the host... The snapshot is consumed by the resume - pause again to take a new one
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshot is memory+disk but single-use and resumes the same sandbox only; not a fork mechanism that boots new, independent running clones.

wake_on_request.quote: auto_resume: When True, any exec or file call on a paused sandbox resumes it automatically first, then runs... and an HTTP request to one of its public preview URLs wakes it the same way, so a parked dev server comes back on the first browser hit.

persistent_disk.quote: A persistent volume is a named disk that survives a sandbox and follows you to the next one. Attach it and it mounts at /persist
persistent_disk.note: /workspace and /tmp are RAM-backed and lost on terminate; /persist volumes survive.

auto_stop_idle.quote: on_timeout: What happens at the deadline: "kill" (default) terminates the sandbox; "pause" snapshots it so a later Sandbox.resume() continues where it left off. Paid tiers always pause; the free tier falls back to terminate at the snapshot cap.
auto_stop_idle.note: Behavior is a fixed countdown timeout (extendable via set_timeout) rather than true activity-based idle detection, but functionally auto-sleeps/terminates an unattended sandbox.

live_resize.quote:
| Size | vCPU | Memory | Availability |
| small | 1 vCPU | 1 GB RAM | default size |
| medium | 2 vCPU | 4 GB RAM | paid tiers |
| large | 4 vCPU | 8 GB RAM | paid tiers |
live_resize.note: Size is fixed at create time; no API to change vCPU/RAM of a running sandbox was found.

agent_harnesses.quote: A plain npm install lands in the writable workspace and takes a few seconds. Skip this step entirely by baking the install into a custom template (step 6).
agent_harnesses.note: Claude Code is documented as a guide you install yourself (npm install / exec), not a preinstalled harness template shipped by orkestr.

own_agent_api.quote: You give a Worker an objective and orkestr runs the agent for you - on demand, on a schedule, or in reaction to an event - driven by your own model. Every action is recorded.
own_agent_api.note: Workers is orkestr's own scoped ops/task agent (roles, skills, memory, approvals) driven via the console/API, distinct from the sandbox runtime and from bringing your own coding harness.

lang_python.quote: python-3.12 - the default. Python 3.12 with pip, development headers and a C/C++ toolchain

lang_node.quote: node-22 - Node.js 22 with npm, a bundled Python and the build toolchain (so node-gyp native addons compile)

public_ipv4.quote: Call sbx.get_host(port)... and you get back a hostname of the form <port>-<id>.sbx.orkestr.run
public_ipv4.note: Ports are exposed via hostname-based preview URLs, not a dedicated public IPv4 address per sandbox.

static_egress_ip.quote: Every mode supports pause and resume - a networked sandbox's IP is held across the pause and restored on resume
static_egress_ip.note: The IP is stable only for that one sandbox's own lifetime/pause-resume cycle; no documented account-level fixed outbound IP for allowlisting across sandboxes.

gpu.quote:
| Size | vCPU | Memory | Availability |
| small | 1 vCPU | 1 GB RAM |
| medium | 2 vCPU | 4 GB RAM |
| large | 4 vCPU | 8 GB RAM |
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only CPU vCPU/RAM sizes are documented; no GPU size or option.

windows.quote: Sandboxes run a stripped-down Linux guest with one of the supported base images: Python 3.12 (full or bare), Node 22, or a real Debian 12
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Linux-only sandbox).

macos.quote: Sandboxes run a stripped-down Linux guest with one of the supported base images: Python 3.12 (full or bare), Node 22, or a real Debian 12
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Linux-only sandbox).

self_host.quote: orkestr is operated by WhiteCloud Project S.R.L., a company registered in Romania (EU)... Sandboxes are placed in one of our EU regions
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. orkestr is a managed multi-tenant SaaS; no self-hosted/on-prem distribution documented.

byoc.quote: Sandboxes are placed in one of our EU regions - you can pin one with the region parameter at create time, or let the control plane pick.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Regions are orkestr's own EU datacenters (Hetzner/OVH), not customer cloud accounts.

open_source.quote: Security at orkestr... Every app deployed on orkestr is protected by multiple layers of security
open_source.note: No OSI-license / open-source-core claim found anywhere in the docs, pricing, or security pages; proprietary managed platform.

soc2.quote: EU Hosting & GDPR: Your data never leaves the European Union... GDPR-compliant by design, Article 28 DPA on request.
soc2.note: Compliance messaging covers only GDPR/EU residency; no SOC 2 attestation mentioned on the security, trust, or compliance pages.

hipaa.quote: EU Hosting & GDPR: Your data never leaves the European Union... GDPR-compliant by design, Article 28 DPA on request.
hipaa.note: No HIPAA/BAA mention anywhere; compliance focus is GDPR-only.

sso.quote: Enterprise ... Everything in Pro, plus: Dedicated single-tenant EU nodes, SSO / SAML + audit logs, 99.9% uptime SLA
sso.note: SSO/SAML is an Enterprise-plan feature of the platform account (which sandboxes run under), not available on Free/Pay-as-you-go.

docker_inside.quote: Every sandbox is its own virtual machine with its own kernel, not a container sharing a host kernel. There is no shared container runtime and no syscall surface between tenants.
docker_inside.note: derived: each sandbox is a full VM with its own kernel and root access (recipe/build steps run as root, apt-get works on the debian-12 base), which is the condition the product itself states enables normal Linux tooling; running a container runtime (e.g. dockerd via apt-get install docker.io) is not blocked by anything documented, but no page explicitly confirms Docker/containers running inside a sandbox, so this is inferred rather than directly stated.

nested_virt.quote: orkestr Sandboxes are hardware-isolated, ephemeral Linux VMs you can spin up from any agent loop. Designed for AI agents that need to run untrusted code, build artifacts, run tests, or operate a stateful development environment without touching your own infrastructure.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Docs describe sandboxes as lightweight, ~200-300ms-boot ephemeral VMs for running code/scripts/builds, not as bare-metal-like environments exposing /dev/kvm for running further VMs/emulators inside; no page mentions nested virtualization or /dev/kvm passthrough.

arm64.quote: The Python and Node bases are glibc-based, not musl. manylinux Python wheels and glibc-built Node native modules install and run without falling back to slow source builds - pip install and npm install behave the way they do on a normal Linux box.
arm64.note: not offered: no ARM/aarch64 option is documented anywhere on the sandboxes product, docs, pricing, or base-images pages; only a single set of base images/architecture is offered from EU (Germany/Finland) data centers with no architecture selector in the create-sandbox API.

usage_api.quote: GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/metrics requires sandboxes:read. Returns the latest CPU and memory reading plus a rolling ~60s window of one-second samples (a sparkline in one call) and the sandbox's lifetime totals. The response includes lifetime: { cpu_seconds: X, gb_seconds: Y }.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: no; Billable usage is available per-sandbox via GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/metrics, which returns cpu_seconds and gb_seconds (the billed quantities). Sandboxes can be listed and filtered by metadata using GET /v1/sandboxes?metadata[key]=value to group by project/tag. Individual metrics must be polled per sandbox id and aggregated by caller.
